haiku-low.q1: In step 4, after the new colour is confirmed idle and before any new instance starts, by one job. The release still serving traffic (the old release) must work on the migrated schema, since migrations are additive.
haiku-low.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that uses the column or table is retired.
haiku-low.q3: All 4 instances must pass /healthz 3 times in a row, and smoke tests must pass, within 10 minutes of instances_started_at. If not, the pipeline aborts: new instances stop, listener untouched.
haiku-low.q4: One API call repoints the public listener from the old target group to the new one, with no gradual shift. The pipeline reads the listener back to confirm the switch.
haiku-low.q5: The 5xx rate exceeding 1% over any 5-minute window, with at least 100 requests. Rollback repoints the listener to the old colour and stops the new colour's instances. Migrations are left applied.
haiku-low.q6: Until 30 minutes after the switch, while phase is watching or soaking; manual rollback can run then. Afterwards, a problem is handled by a normal deploy of previous_release via revert or re-run, with migrations not reversed.
haiku-low.q7: Migrations finished before the failure stay applied, each in its own transaction; they are additive, so safe. The deploy sets phase failed, alerts the author and stops. Listener untouched, live colour keeps serving; author fixes via new merge.
haiku-low.q8: The listener's target group is the only source of truth: the pipeline reads it to set old and new colours, then compares with deploy-state.json in versioned artifact storage. Disagreement stops the pipeline and alerts an engineer.
haiku-low.q9: The CI concurrency lock catalog-web-deploy allows one deploy at a time. It is held from step 2 until the deploy finishes, including the 30-minute wait before old colour shutdown. Only the newest queued merge runs.
haiku-low.q10: Smoke tests call the new colour's instances directly through the new target group's internal addresses, not the public listener, so no user traffic is involved.
haiku-low.q11: One job in CI runs the release's migrations in step 4, each in its own transaction. Migrations must be safe to re-run; whether one ran is read from the database's migrations table.
haiku-low.q12: After an abort or rollback, the new colour's instances are stopped. The next deploy's step 3 stops any remaining instances and confirms the target group is empty before proceeding.

sonnet.q1: Step 4, after the new colour is confirmed idle (step 3) and before any new instance starts. The release now serving traffic (old release) must keep working on the migrated schema, which is why migrations must be additive.
sonnet.q2: Only in a later release, after the release that uses the column or table is retired. Migrations that drop or rename fail the build in step 1.
sonnet.q3: All 4 new instances must each pass /healthz 3 times in a row (checked every 10 seconds, all healthy at the same time), and the smoke tests must pass, with steps 6 and 7 together finishing within 10 minutes of instances_started_at. If not, the deploy aborts: new instances are stopped, phase = aborted, the author is alerted, the lock is released, the listener is untouched and migrations stay applied.
sonnet.q4: In one step. One API call repoints the public load balancer listener from the old target group to the new one, with no gradual shift. The pipeline then reads the listener back to confirm.
sonnet.q5: Trigger: the 5xx rate goes above 1% over any rolling 5-minute window (evaluated every 60 seconds, windows with fewer than 100 requests are not evaluated). Changes: writes phase = rolled_back first (blocks step 11 and other rollbacks), checks the 4 old instances are healthy, repoints the listener back to the old target group, stops the new colour's instances after the deregistration delay, alerts the author and releases the lock. Left alone: migrations stay applied and are never reversed.
sonnet.q6: For 30 minutes after the switch (until old_colour_shutdown_at, while the old colour is running), via the manual rollback job when phase is watching or soaking. After the old colour is shut down, a rollback is a normal deploy of previous_release (merge a revert or re-run the pipeline for previous_release), steps 1 to 12.
sonnet.q7: Migrations that finished before the failure stay applied, which is safe because they are additive. Each migration runs in its own transaction. The pipeline sets phase = failed, alerts the author and stops. No new instance has started and the listener is untouched, so the live colour keeps serving. The author fixes it with a new merge.
sonnet.q8: The load balancer's public listener is the source of truth: step 2 reads which target group it points at, sets old_colour to that colour and new_colour to the other. It is recorded in the deploy state record (catalog-web/deploy-state.json) as old_colour and new_colour. If the listener and the record disagree, the pipeline alerts an engineer and stops.
sonnet.q9: The deploy lock, a CI concurrency group named catalog-web-deploy. It is held from step 2 until the deploy finishes, including the 30-minute wait before the old colour shuts down. Merges during that time queue, and only the newest queued merge runs.
sonnet.q10: The smoke tests call the new colour's instances directly through the new target group's internal addresses. The listener still points at the old target group, so no user traffic is involved.
sonnet.q11: One job (step 4) runs the release's migrations against the shared database, each in its own transaction, with a 10-minute limit. Once-per-deploy comes from this being a single job applied before any new instance starts, with the deploy lock allowing one deploy at a time. Migrations must also be safe to re-run. Whether a migration ran is read from the database's migrations table.
sonnet.q12: On an abort, the pipeline stops the new instances. On a rollback, it stops them after the deregistration delay. Either way the new colour is left with no instances (idle). The next deploy's step 3 checks the new colour is idle: it stops any leftover instances, and fails if they cannot be stopped or the target group is the listener's target.
